title: How to Make Towels Soft Again

seo.title: How to Make Towels Soft Again
seo.meta_description: Towels often become stiff because of excess detergent, hard-water minerals, fabric-softener buildup, or drying that mats the loops.
seo.search_intent: Use a practical, safe method to make Towels Soft Again, with clear checks, limits, and next steps.

excerpt: Towels often become stiff because of excess detergent, hard-water minerals, fabric-softener buildup, or drying that mats the loops. Restoring softness means removing residue and fixing the routine rather than adding more softener.
content_html:
Towels often become stiff because of excess detergent, hard-water minerals, fabric-softener buildup, or drying that mats the loops. Restoring softness means removing residue and fixing the routine rather than adding more softener.

Reduce detergent dosing on the next wash

A load with lots of suds is not necessarily cleaner and can retain detergent in the fibers. Use the amount recommended for load size, water hardness, and soil level.

Avoid fabric-softener buildup on towel loops

Fabric softener coats fibers to create a smooth feel, but excess can reduce absorbency and build up over time. If you use it, follow the dose; many towels improve when softener is reduced or skipped for several washes.

Rinse thoroughly when buildup is suspected

An extra rinse can help after detergent overdosing if the washer allows it. Do not mix vinegar with bleach or use additives the machine manufacturer advises against.

Shake towels out and avoid over-drying

Shaking towels before and after drying helps separate the loops. Dry at the care-label temperature and avoid running the cycle long after they are dry because excess heat can stiffen fibers and damage decorative elastic or trim.
